title: A&J FAQ
section: What days should I fly in for the celebration?
text:
What days should I fly in for the celebration?
Guests are encouraged to arrive Wednesday or Thursday afternoon to be part of all of the events.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What airport should I fly into?
text:
What airport should I fly into?
Santa Marta’s international airport is Simón Bolívar International Airport (SMR). There aren’t any direct flights from the US, but there are one stop flights from the Miami/Ft. Lauderdale and the New York area with reasonably short layovers in Bogota or Panama. Simón Bolívar International Airport (SMR) is 10 minutes from the Pozos Colorados district (where the wedding party will be staying). Uber and local taxis are easily accessible from the airport.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What is the dress code for the wedding?
text:
What is the dress code for the wedding?
Our goal is to have our guests be comfortable and dress beach formal to accommodate the warm weather. Think light, airy fabrics that work well in a tropical climate and complement a celebration by the beach.
We encourage outfits that are both elegant and comfortable. Flowing silhouettes, breathable materials, and natural details are all great options.
For shoes, consider wedges, platforms, and stable dress shoes rather than thin heeled shoes in order to feel comfortable walking on varying floor surfaces, textures, and prepare for an evening of dancing!
Accessories are encouraged to help show personality and bring together your beach formal looks.

title: A&J FAQ
section: Will the ceremony reception be indoors or outdoors?
text:
Will the ceremony reception be indoors or outdoors?
The ceremony and reception will be held outdoors.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What’s the weather like in December?
text:
What’s the weather like in December?
Daytime highs range between 85–90°F (29–32°C) with nighttime lows between 73–77°F (23–25°C) with humidity throughout the day. Make sure to bring your sunscreen and light layers for ocean breezes at night!

title: A&J FAQ
text:
Is Santa Marta generally safe?
Yes! Like any foreign destination, we recommend standard precautions – but Santa Marta is a lovely coastal town known for its relaxed vibe, friendly locals, and beautiful landscapes. As long as you stay aware of your surroundings, you’ll be able to enjoy all the beauty the city has to offer.

title: A&J FAQ
section: Is Uber available in Santa Marta?
text:
Is Uber available in Santa Marta?
Yes, uber is easily accessible in Santa Marta.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What areas of town should we look into?
text:
What areas of town should we look into?
The wedding party will be staying in Pozos Colorado. It is a quieter beachfront area with beautiful views, plenty of hotel options, and a more peaceful vibe. It is also ~10-15 minutes away from the airport, the wedding venue, and downtown Santa Marta. Other options –

Centro Histórico (~30 minutes from the airport). It’s busier and farther from the beach, but walkable.

El Rodadero (~25 minutes from the airport) is lively and full of restaurants and nightlife although it can be very touristy.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What are some fun things to do in Santa Marta?
text:
What are some fun things to do in Santa Marta?
– Excursions –

Tayrona National Natural Park - one of Colombia’s most breathtaking national parks with luscious, tropical hikes and stunning beaches.

Minca - a tiny town tucked into the Sierra Nevada mountains. Visit eco-lodges, tour coffee farms, and swim in the Pozo Azul waterfall.

Taganga - bohemian and budget friendly side of town that offers scuba diving and snorkeling excursions.

– Restaurants –

Lulo Café Bar de Jugos, Altamar Café, Donde Chucho, Batey, Ouzu, Santa Mesa, BK Restaurante

– Things to See –

El Pibe Valderrama statue outside the Estadio Eduardo Santos.

Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino – Hacienda where Simón Bolivar spent his last days.

Museo del Oro Tairona, Casa de la Aduana – Museum of gold housed in the oldest surviving colonial-era building in Colombia.

title: A&J FAQ
section: Do I need a visa to visit Colombia? Any passport requirements?
text:
Do I need a visa to visit Colombia? Any passport requirements?
Most visitors from the U.S., Canada, and the EU don’t need a visa—just a valid passport. Please ensure your passport is not set to expire less than six months post December 2025.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What is the local currency in Colombia?
text:
What is the local currency in Colombia?
The local currency in Colombia is the Colombian Peso (COP). Credit/debit cards are widely accepted and ATMs are available around town. Cash is useful for taxi, tips, markets, and street vendors.

title: Our Story
text:
SO WE MET IN CHEMISTRY










We were lab partners at our high school chemistry class and quickly became friends. After graduation, we kept in touch even when Juan moved to New York in 2011. The signs were always there, like that New Year’s sunrise in South Beach or that night in the party bus rolling through the streets of Manhattan.  It wasn’t until Andrea moved to New York that our romantic story unfolded. Twenty years since we met, it still feels like we’re those two kids in chemistry.  Now, just in love and ready for our next chapter.

title: A&J FAQ
text: Beach Club

title: A&J FAQ
text:
Where is Inca Inca?
A beach club located in Playa Inca Inca. Playa Inca Inca is a small, secluded beach just outside El Rodadero (about a 5-minute boat ride).

title: A&J FAQ
section: What is the attire for the beach club?
text:
What is the attire for the beach club?
The attire is beach wear. We highly recommend to bring your swimsuits! This is one of Santa Marta’s best semi-private beaches ideal for swimming and laying out on the sand, if that’s what you wish.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What is the vibe for the event?
text:
What is the vibe for the event?
Whether you’re up for a swim, some sun, or just relaxing by the beach, Inca Inca beach club offers the ideal spot to enjoy Santa Marta’s coast.

title: A&J FAQ
text:
How do we get there?
There are day-pass tours from Rodadero (meeting point Cra. 1 #7-69, El Rodadero). We are offering complimentary round-trip transportation from the Hilton Santa Marta to El Rodadero (at 12:00 PM and 6:15 PM), and complimentary round trip transportation to Inca Inca.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What time do I have to be there?
text:
What time do I have to be there?
If you wish to leave with the wedding party, the shuttle will be departing from the Hilton Santa Marta (Pozos Colorados) to El Rodadero beach at 12:00 PM on Saturday, December 6th. We will be boarding the Taximarino to Inca Inca around 12:30 - 12:45 pm.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What if I don’t make it in time for the Taximarino?
text:
What if I don’t make it in time for the Taximarino?
No worries – there are plenty of vendors that provide transportation by boat. Head to the main pier (Muelle Turístico de El Rodadero) and ask for boats going to Playa Inca Inca. The cost is usually 10,000-20,000 COP (~ $2-5 USD) round trip. The trip is 5-10 minutes by water and run frequently. Please bring cash as card payments with beachside vendors are rare.

title: A&J FAQ
section: Will there be food and bevarages?
text:
Will there be food and bevarages?
Yes! The beach club has a full bar and a buffet menu. Card payments are acceptable.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What are the hours of the event?
text:
What are the hours of the event?
The post-wedding beach event kicks off at 1 PM with a private catamaran taking guests back at 6 PM. If guests wish to leave before 6 PM, there will be a Taximarino that can take guests back at 2 PM or 4 pm. After 4 PM, the only transportation available is the catamaran at 6 PM. Round-trip ransportation via the Taximarino and/or private catamaran is complimentary for our guests.

title: A&J FAQ
section: Will there be transportation provided for the wedding events?
text:
Will there be transportation provided for the wedding events?
Transportation will be provided for our wedding events and will be departing / returning to the Hilton Santa Marta (Pozos Colorado).
Ubers/taxis are also easily accessible for anyone who is not staying in the Hilton Santa Marta. See events tab for more details on the meet times/departures from the hotel.

title: A&J FAQ
section: What if I don’t make it to the Rodadero by 12:45 PM?
text:
What if I don’t make it to the Rodadero by 12:45 PM?
No worries — the Taximarino boats depart from Rodadero to Inca Inca every 15–30 minutes. Your names will be shared with the Taximarino team, so you can arrive at Inca Inca at any time that works best for you. Be sure to mention “Andrea y Juan post-boda event” upon check-in. The Taximarino departs from the main pier (Muelle Turístico de El Rodadero).
